runtime_rules_logging_off.method: 1200 typed action-result events through real session/router, first 100 excluded

minilm_provider_synthetic.method: Single provider, synthetic visible-body input, 20 warmup calls, two CPU threads
minilm_provider_synthetic.rss_units: bytes on macOS; KiB on Linux
minilm_provider_synthetic.limitations: Not a concurrent multi-actor or full-game load test; file writes use OS buffering

interpretation: Microsecond-level Runtime overhead in this probe; optional inference is millisecond-scale. Rules alone remain faster than neural inference.
limitations: Single-run microbenchmarks have timing noise; these are not absolute service-level guarantees.
Provider probe is a short synthetic input, not the latency of a whole match or all input lengths.

cold_start_async.method: Fresh Python process, async model factory, 10ms heartbeat probe

four_live_runtimes.scenario: Four simultaneous MiniLM agents during a real discussion phase
four_live_runtimes.scope: Runtime processes including model and Python; Unity clients are not included; RSS is a snapshot, not peak

cold_start_fix: Initial synchronous construction blocked the loop about 8 seconds with four live clients and caused heartbeat disconnection. Registry async creation now loads only the model in a thread; collector setup stays on the loop.
live_latency_scope: Four agents and real Unity clients on this Mac; includes projection/thread scheduling; part of validation ran concurrently.
